Silk Board floods because it sits at the bottom of a bowl. 🥣

Bangalore Decoded.

⛰️ A valley floor
Silk Board junction sits on a valley floor. Deccan Herald reported in 2017 that the valley narrows right at the junction, from the Adugodi side and the Madiwala-BTM Layout side, and that the junction's flooding is blamed on this squeeze.

🌧️ Four directions
In May 2025, Deccan Herald called Central Silk Board junction a "chronic flood-prone spot where water from four directions converges".

🌊 The lake next door
Madiwala lake's overflow naturally runs east to Agara lake, then on to Bellandur and Varthur.

🛣️ Then we built in it
The Outer Ring Road stretch near Madiwala lake is built on that valley. Then came the double-decker flyover and a metro station.

📅 May 2025
After heavy rain on 18 and 19 May 2025, one side of the road under the double-decker flyover was unusable, and rainwater reached the escalators of the Silk Board metro station, which had not opened yet.

🚇 The pillar
Transport Minister Ramalinga Reddy said Namma Metro blocked drainage on the Madiwala side: "They built a pillar blocking the natural flow of water."

🤯 The part most people don't know
Maheshwar Rao, then BBMP chief commissioner and also managing director of Namma Metro (BMRCL), said the Silk Board area "forms a bowl-like depression, causing water to flow backward into the station during heavy rains" (NewsKarnataka). To The Times of India he said the area forms a "saucer" near the station, and water pushes back into it when the stormwater drain is full.
